# Lab 18.9: Encryption: CMEK & Column-Level AEAD

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Cloud KMS key, let BigQuery use it, and make it the default encryption key for a dataset (CMEK). Then encrypt single column values with AEAD functions.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a key ring and key in the same location as the data.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable cloudkms.googleapis.com
gcloud kms keyrings create lab-ring --location=us
gcloud kms keys create bq-key --keyring=lab-ring --location=us \
  --purpose=encryption --protection-level=software</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   A `US` dataset needs a key in the `us` multi-region. Use `--protection-level=hsm` for keys in Cloud HSM.

2. **[CLI] Let the BigQuery service agent use the key.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq show --encryption_service_account
PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)")
BQ_SA=bq-$PROJECT_NUMBER@bigquery-encryption.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding bq-key --keyring=lab-ring --location=us \
  --member=serviceAccount:$BQ_SA --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   This grants **Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter** to the service agent, not to people.

3. **[Console] Create a dataset with CMEK as the default.** **Create dataset** → `lab18_cmek`, location **US** → **Advanced options → Customer-managed encryption key** → choose `bq-key`. The same with the CLI:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset \
  --default_kms_key=projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us/keyRings/lab-ring/cryptoKeys/bq-key \
  $PROJECT_ID:lab18_cmek</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[CLI] Create a table and check its key.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'CREATE TABLE lab18_cmek.secret_sales AS SELECT * FROM lab18.sales'
bq show --format=prettyjson lab18_cmek.secret_sales | grep kmsKeyName</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[SQL] Column-level encryption with AEAD.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab18.keys AS
SELECT 'customer_1' AS key_id, KEYS.NEW_KEYSET('AEAD_AES_GCM_256') AS keyset;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab18.cards AS
SELECT 'customer_1' AS customer, AEAD.ENCRYPT(k.keyset, '4111-1111-1111-1111', 'customer_1') AS card_enc
FROM lab18.keys k WHERE key_id = 'customer_1';

SELECT c.customer, AEAD.DECRYPT_STRING(k.keyset, c.card_enc, c.customer) AS card
FROM lab18.cards c JOIN lab18.keys k ON k.key_id = c.customer;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **[SQL] Crypto-deletion.** Delete the customer's key; their data can never be decrypted again:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">DELETE FROM lab18.keys WHERE key_id = 'customer_1';</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


7. **[Console] See key usage.** In **Security → Key Management**, open `bq-key` and look at its key usage view, which lists the resources the key protects. Keep the key for the next labs.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Table encryption | With your key, `bq-key` |
| Who uses the key | BigQuery encryption service agent |
| Key location | Must match the data location (`us` for `US`) |
| AEAD | Per-value encryption; deleting the keyset makes data unreadable |
